report.source_text: We treated with rifabutin 300 mg/day plus clarithromycin 800 mg/day. Due to liver dysfunction 1 month after starting the treatment, the regimen was changed to moxifloxacin 400 mg/day plus clarithromycin 800 mg/day. Three months later, the patient developed nausea due to moxifloxacin. The treatment was then switched to linezolid 1200 mg/day and clarithromycin. Following these changes, there were no further complications, and the skin findings demonstrated a trend of improvement. The nodule flattened, and the postinflammatory pigmentation had faded over 7 months

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old aquarium management worker presented with a 2-year history of progressive skin lesions (nodules and ulcer) on the right upper extremity (forearm and thumb) following an arm injury sustained while working with aquariums. Initial clinical evaluation revealed a 3-cm nodule on the radial side of the right forearm with crusted surface and mild erythema, and a 1-cm nodule near the proximal phalanx of the right thumb. T-SPOT.TB testing was positive. An initial excisional biopsy performed 3 months prior to presentation yielded negative cultures and PCR for M. tuberculosis. A second excisional biopsy was subsequently performed, showing histopathology with moderate inflammatory infiltration but without epithelioid granulomas, multinucleated giant cells, or necrosis. DNA extraction followed by PCR sequencing from the second biopsy specimen confirmed M. marinum. Chest CT with contrast ruled out pulmonary involvement and lymphadenopathy. Treatment was initiated with rifabutin 300 mg/day plus clarithromycin 800 mg/day, but was modified to moxifloxacin 400 mg/day plus clarithromycin due to liver dysfunction at 1 month. After the patient developed nausea from moxifloxacin at 3 months, the regimen was changed to linezolid 1200 mg/day plus clarithromycin. With this final regimen, the patient experienced clinical improvement with flattening of the nodule and fading of postinflammatory pigmentation over 7 months of follow-up.
